# GitHub Actions and S3 {.unnumbered} :::: {.callout-warning collapse='false' appearance='default' icon='false'} ## [Caution]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.25em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 1.00em; color: #282b2d;'} This section is being revised. Thank you for your patience. ::: :::: ## Automating Model Deployment with GitHub Actions GitHub Actions can automatically build and publish our `vetiver` models to S3 whenever we push changes. In this section I'll cover setting up AWS credentials as repository secrets and creating a workflow to automate the model publishing process. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'GitHub Actions Automated Deployment' %%| fig-width: 7.0 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'monospace'}}}%% graph TD Push["Developer
Pushes to main"] --> GHA["GitHub
Actions"] GHA --> Build["Build Models
(py_model, r_model)"] Build --> Auth["Configure AWS
Credentials"] Auth --> Upload["Upload to S3
with pins"] Upload --> Success["Models
Published"] style Push fill:#5B8C5A,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style GHA fill:#E8A33D,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style Build fill:#1B2A41,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style Auth fill:#2A6F77,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style Upload fill:#D2562B,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style Success fill:#5B8C5A,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff ``` ## Setting up GitHub Secrets First, we need to add the following secrets to the GitHub repository (Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions): 1. `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`: Your AWS access key ID from the `mjfrigaard-cli` IAM user 2. `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`: Your AWS secret access key 3. `AWS_REGION`: Your AWS region (e.g., `us-east-1`) These credentials belong to the `mjfrigaard-cli` IAM user with `AmazonS3FullAccess` permissions (i.e., the same user for local AWS CLI configuration). ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'GitHub Secrets Flow' %%| fig-width: 7.0 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'monospace'}}}%% graph TD Secrets["GitHub Repository
Secrets"] Secrets --> AccessKey["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] Secrets --> SecretKey["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] Secrets --> Region["AWS_REGION"] AccessKey --> Workflow["Workflow Job
(aws-actions/
configure-aws-
credentials)"] SecretKey --> Workflow Region --> Workflow Workflow --> S3["Temporary AWS
Credentials"] S3 --> Access["Access to S3"] style Secrets fill:#D2562B,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style AccessKey fill:#1B2A41,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style SecretKey fill:#1B2A41,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style Region fill:#1B2A41,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style Workflow fill:#E8A33D,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style S3 fill:#2A6F77,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff style Access fill:#5B8C5A,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff ``` ## GitHub Actions Workflow File Next, we create `.github/workflows/publish.yml` to build and publish the models to our S3 bucjet. The models are automatically versioned by `vetiver` (e.g., `20260710T065220Z-91fdd`), so we're creating a new version in S3 with each workflow run. ```yaml name: Publish Models to S3 on: push: branches: [lab07-s3] #<1> paths: - '_labs/lab07/py_model.qmd' - '_labs/lab07/r_model.qmd' - '.github/workflows/publish.yml' jobs: publish-models: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Check out repository #<2> uses: actions/checkout@v4 #<2> - name: Configure AWS credentials #<3> uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4 with: aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }} aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }} aws-region: ${{ secrets.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1' }} #<3> - name: Set up Python #<4> uses: actions/setup-python@v5 with: python-version: '3.12' - name: Set up R uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2 with: r-version: '4.4' - name: Install Python dependencies working-directory: ./_labs/lab07 run: | python -m pip install --upgrade pip pip install -r Python/requirements.txt pins vetiver python-dotenv - name: Install R dependencies working-directory: ./_labs/lab07 run: | R -e "install.packages(c('vetiver', 'pins', 'plumber2', 'paws.storage'))" #<4> - name: Build and publish Python model #<5> working-directory: ./_labs/lab07 env: USE_S3: 'true' AWS_REGION: ${{ secrets.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1' }} PINS_ALLOW_PICKLE_READ: '1' run: | python py_model.py - name: Build and publish R model working-directory: ./_labs/lab07 env: USE_S3: 'true' AWS_REGION: ${{ secrets.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1' }} run: | Rscript r_model.R #<5> ``` 1. **Trigger**: Runs when `py_model.qmd`, `r_model.qmd`, or this workflow file changes on the `lab07-s3` branch 2. **Checkout**: Downloads the latest code from the repository 3. **AWS Auth**: Uses `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` to set up temporary AWS credentials from GitHub secrets (no long-lived keys stored in the runner) 4. **Setup**: Installs Python 3.12 and R 4.4 with required dependencies 5. **Build & Publish**: Runs `py_model.py` and `r_model.R` with `USE_S3=true` environment variable, which causes the model scripts to write directly to S3 Publishing via GitHub Actions automate the model deployment without any permanent AWS credentials sitting in the repository. ## Developing on the `lab07-s3` Branch Now, I want to keep the `main` branch reserved for the Quarto book rendering, so any model changes will go in the `lab07-s3` branch (which triggers the model publishing workflow). Since I've already been developing on `main`, I'll need to create and switch to the `lab07-s3` branch: First I'll create/check out the `lab07-s3` branch from `main`: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} git checkout -b lab07-s3 ``` ::: And push the new branch to GitHub: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} git push -u origin lab07-s3 ``` ::: Once on the `lab07-s3` branch, I'll need to follow this process: ### Make changes Make changes to the model files (i.e., `_labs/lab07/py_model.qmd` or `_labs/lab07/r_model.qmd`) ### Test changes (locally) To test changes locally, I'll need to set the environment variables for S3 (or use local for testing): ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} export USE_S3=false # or true if testing S3 locally ``` ::: Then render/run the files with the changes ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} quarto render py_model.qmd # or Rscript r_model.R ``` ::: ### Commit changes Commit the changes (be specific about the files): ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} git add _labs/lab07/py_model.qmd _labs/lab07/r_model.qmd git commit -m "Update model configuration or training logic" ``` ::: ### Push changes Push to the `lab07-s3` branch: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} git push origin lab07-s3 ``` ::: GitHub Actions will automatically detects the `push` to `lab07-s3`, build the models using the latest code, and publish the versioned models to S3 with AWS credentials from secrets. ### Verify We can verify the models were published using: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} # List files in S3 aws s3 ls s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/ --recursive --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: ### Merge to `main` Don't forget to merge to `main` if the changes also belong in the book. ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} git checkout main git merge lab07-s3 git push origin main ``` ::: Then publish the book: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} quarto publish gh-pages ``` :::
